learningObjective: Explain how SCCP achieves greater precision than plain constant propagation by combining constant propagation with reachability analysis.

canonicalClaims.claim: Sparse Conditional Constant Propagation (SCCP) maintains two lattices — variable values and edge reachability — and propagates constants only along edges proven reachable, yielding higher precision than plain constant propagation on branchy code.
nonImplications: Does not imply SCCP always outperforms plain propagation; when no conditions are constant, they coincide.
Does not imply SCCP is unbounded in analysis time; it iterates lattices to fixpoint.

misconceptions.claim: Plain constant propagation can skip unreachable branches via heuristics.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Plain constant propagation merges all reaching definitions without proving reachability; it does not use branch conditions.

misconceptions.claim: SCCP differs from plain constant propagation only in loops.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SCCP's edge-reachability lattice benefits any branchy code where a constant condition prunes an infeasible path.

misconceptions.claim: SCCP defaults to a branch when the condition is not constant.
misconceptions.whyWrong: When the branch condition is non-constant, both successor edges are marked reachable and propagation proceeds as in plain analysis.

implementationFacts: SCCP uses two worklists: one for flow edges, one for SSA edges.
LLVM implements SCCP in llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/SCCP.cpp; also IPSCCP for interprocedural.
performanceScenarios: SCCP eliminates dead branches based on constant conditions; important for template-heavy or macro-expanded code with lots of compile-time constants.
